skill_traces.query:
Evan: Hey Sam, hope you're doing good. Wanted to share some amazing news - my partner is pregnant! We're so excited! It's been a while since we had a kiddo around.
Sam: Congrats, Ev! That's great news! Parenthood is so amazing. How are you feeling about it?
Evan: So excited and a bit nervous! It's been a while since I had a toddler around but I'm really looking forward to it. Parenthood is so rewarding. I still remember when my first child was born, the joy was amazing. Looking forward to witness the miracle of life and build more memories with my family!
Sam: Wow, you're gonna be an amazing parent! Treasure those memories, they're truly special.
Evan: Thanks Sam! Absolutely. Talking of memories, I want to show you this. It's a collage of some of our top family memories. Each photo has an amazing moment - birthdays, holidays, vacations - so good to look back and recall all the great times we had.
Sam: That's so lovely, Evan. Your family looks so happy. What's the story behind that sign in the center?
Evan: Oh, that one? It's from our trip to Banff. We have this sign in the frame that says 'Bring it on Home' - it's our family's motto, always reminding us of the importance of togetherness, no matter where we are.
Sam: That's really touching, Evan. It's important to have something that keeps the family bond strong.
Evan: Absolutely, Sam. My family means the world to me. They're my rock. I'm looking forward to expanding our family and creating even more beautiful memories.
Sam: That's wonderful to hear, Evan! It's clear how much you value your family. Are you thinking of any specific plans or events to add to that collage?
Evan: Thanks, Sam! Yeah, we're planning a big family reunion next summer. It's going to be a blast and a perfect opportunity to add to our collage.
Sam: Sounds fantastic! If you need any tips on organizing such a big event, just let me know. I'm always here to support and celebrate your family's milestones.
Evan: Thanks, Sam! Your support means a lot. I'll keep you updated. Take care, bye!
Sam: Take care, Evan! Can't wait to hear about it. Bye!
Evan: Bye Sam. I'll definitely keep you updated. Thanks for the kind words and support. Take care!

selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

selected.name: Attribute Memories to Actual Speaker
selected.description: When extracting profile or preference memories from multi-party conversations, attribute each statement to the speaker who uttered it, not to another mentioned participant.
content: During extraction, treat each speaker's message as its own evidence unit: create a separate candidate per message and per speaker, and set the memory's subject to the speaker who uttered that message.
Do not merge opinions from different speakers into a single memory unless the speakers explicitly state the view jointly (e.g., 'we both like').
When a message contains a self-disclosure (e.g., 'I also have...', 'Yes, I...'), create a separate candidate for that speaker even if the message also contains a question or reply.
If the message text clearly attributes the preference to someone else (e.g., 'Tim loves...'), use that person only then; otherwise default to the speaker.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation involves multiple speakers, and each message needs to be attributed to the speaker who uttered it, ensuring accurate memory creation for each individual.

content: During extraction, treat statements like 'X sparked ideas for my [project]' as a plan/state memory candidate.
Do not skip a turn just because it contains no direct question; extract motivation and project details from casual narrative.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Start of Specific Creative Work
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user confirms starting or recently beginning a specific creative work.
content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.
